sources.name: USACE National Inventory of Dams (NID), public feature service
sources.summary: Read live 2026-11-10 (NID web app text served at nid.sec.usace.army.mil/nid/): 'The NID is publicly available. Regular users include: ... Engineering and construction companies ... Media ... The insurance industry ... Dam and reservoir users'; 'Some dam information is publicly available, while some dam regulatory and oversight programs may restrict access to some of the information' (restricted fields are not in the public service; we read only the public one). The site's only disclaimer is the DoD information-system banner (monitoring consent), with no limit on reuse, advertising, commercial use or caching. 33 U.S.C. 467d: the Secretary 'shall make the inventory ... publicly available'. USACE is a federal agency (17 U.S.C. 105: no copyright in U.S. Government works). Field units from the NID data dictionary in the same app: surface area 'in acres ... at its normal retention level'; normal and maximum storage 'in acre-feet'; dam height 'in feet'; NID height = the largest of dam, structural and hydraulic height. Hazard potential rates the harm if the dam failed, not its condition: not shown. Earlier row (2026-11-09) was off on merit: NID has no full-pool elevation, so it cannot say how full a lake is; this block shows only what NID states about the dam itself and computes no percent full.
sources.credit: Data: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, National Inventory of Dams
sources.evidence: nid.sec.usace.army.mil/nid/ app bundle (FAQ 'Who Uses the NID?', disclaimer modal, field definitions) read 2026-11-10; geospatial.sec.usace.army.mil/dls/rest/services/NID/National_Inventory_of_Dams_Public_Service/FeatureServer/0 queried 2026-11-10 (Buford Dam GA00824); law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/33/467d

sources.name: Environment Agency real-time flood-monitoring API (Beta), England
sources.summary: API reference, read 2026-11-03: 'These APIs are provided as open data under the Open Government Licence with no requirement for registration. If you make use of this data please acknowledge this with the following attribution statement: this uses Environment Agency flood and river level data from the real-time data API (Beta)'. Every reply's meta.licence is OGL v3.0, whose text (nationalarchives.gov.uk, read 2026-11-03) allows exploiting the information 'commercially and non-commercially' with that attribution and a link to the licence. The reference also says the APIs 'should not be relied upon for safety critical applications' and asks for one readings?latest call per 15 min rather than crawling every station. Rainfall reference (/doc/rainfall, read 2026-11-03): same OGL terms, attribution 'this uses Environment Agency rainfall data from the real-time data API (Beta)', tipping bucket gauges, mm totals per 15 min; we read rain in one bulk call a run.

sources.evidence: curl of /doc/reference and /id/stations/4009 meta.licence 2026-11-03; OGL v3.0 page read the same night. Nothing from memory.

sources.summary: 'Most datasets are available under a standard Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence'; data and derivatives must carry Met Eireann's five attribution statements (Copyright Met Eireann; Source met.ie; ...). Not yet read: which datasets (warnings, forecast) fall under it.

sources.name: USACE Corps Water Management System (CWMS) data dissemination
sources.summary: Read 2026-11-09 in the owner's Chrome: 'The CWMS Data Dissemination website is a public accessible map based repository of water resources data that includes elevation, precipitation, storage, and flow status'; 'All data contained herein is preliminary in nature and therefore subject to change. The data is for general information purposes ONLY'. Plus the DoD website banner (monitoring consent). No bar on reuse, ads or caching. Label every value preliminary, USACE.

sources.name: Agency river-use rules (county, city, park and river authority notices)
sources.summary: Ordinances and rules issued by a body with lawmaking power are not copyrightable (Georgia v. Public.Resource.Org, US Supreme Court, 2020-04-27). Other agency notices are quoted under 25 words, word for word, attributed and linked to the agency's page; a page whose own terms bar reuse is not added (data/activity-limits.csv is hand-checked row by row).
